questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I was interested in the country, I were to visit.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. However, I was always nervous about missing a deadline or that there was some information I had missed, because the mobility online interface is a bit confusing, and you had to find different information on different platforms.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received an email from my study abroad advisor.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, but I was lucky that I very early on got on the list for accomadations.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very expensive for the size and the condition of the place. It's my belief, that the university should not make money off of students basic need to have a place to live. The context of the late-stage-capitalist housing market does not help.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to go to the law campus and show my passport. And also do a questionaire at some office. The staff were helpfull.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to find the exact location for registration, but the staff were helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a longer process, I had to try to apply to classes many times before I got classes I could attend. It was not completely transparent to me, which classes I could take and which I could not.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh is an expensive city, so maybe also consider a place in central Europe, if that could be an issue for you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level a bit low compared to my home university. We did not read a lot of theory, which sometimes prevented the classes from reaching a higher analytical level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As I mentioned above, I felt like the level was a bit lower. I had the sense the professors controlled the classes more, whereas I feel like the classes are more student led in UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Reading Latin American Poetry, Islamic and Middle Eastern Cultures, Black Hydro-poetics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Reading Latin American Poetry and Black Hydro-poetics. I would recommend RLA because the I really liked the teaching style, group readings of poems. I would recommend BHP, because the class introduces some interesting analytical and theoretical approaches.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There was nothing in my student accommodation, so I had to buy a duvet, pots, knives, pans etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Maybe public transport. And the accommodation, because it did not even have the basic things for living and for the money the standard was bad. Also laundry.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I really liked the student associations, which offered sports and other activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to join an association and go to protest!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Relax with your friends, maybe go see a castle, have a pint.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't know, tried, but did not succeed. Would love a tip.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language, even though I speak English well, I was surprised at how difficult native speakers found it to understand my different way of speaking.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture, the openness and being very polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't go there for the academia, but for having a nice chill time in a cool, but expensive city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring a sleeping bag.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from friends and familiy when sad.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
